metadata.title: Server Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for defining when a server instance may be treated as an acceptable execution environment for institutional workloads.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Server hardware, hypervisors, virtual machines, bare‑metal systems, host operating systems, and workload execution substrates.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational pattern defining execution‑trust eligibility for server environments within a Zero Trust architecture.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines server execution environments as bounded data‑processing domains whose data handling authority is derived from trust signals and policy, not platform presence.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Primary control catalog governing server identity, access control, configuration management, and integrity (AC, IA, CM, SI families).

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines Zero Trust principles establishing that server execution trust is conditional, continuously evaluated, and revocable.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Establishes platform firmware and host resilience expectations for servers, including detect, protect, and recover capabilities.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines BIOS and boot integrity principles informing server attestation and execution‑trust assumptions.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Extends firmware integrity guidance with authenticated boot requirements applicable to modern server platforms.

metadata.remarks: Server Core defines the minimum trust conditions under which a server may execute institutional workloads. This pattern establishes execution eligibility and trust boundaries but does not evaluate vulnerability posture, configuration drift, runtime behavior, patch compliance, or incident response.

components.title: Server Identity and Accountability
components.description: Ensures server instances are uniquely identifiable and attributable to an owning authority.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Use of unmanaged or unidentified servers to host workloads.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Formal server identity registration establishes accountability.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Servers are uniquely identified prior to participation in institutional systems.
An inventory of authorized server assets is maintained.

components.title: Server Execution Boundary
components.description: Defines the security boundary within which server execution trust is asserted.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through misinterpreted execution context.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit execution boundaries prevent trust overreach.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege applies to workload execution authority.

components.title: Server Platform Integrity Anchor
components.description: Establishes that server execution occurs atop a verifiable and integrity‑anchored platform.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Persistence through firmware, bootloader, or host OS compromise.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Measured boot and hardware roots of trust anchor execution integrity.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Integrity mechanisms detect unauthorized modification of platform components.

components.title: Server Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what Server Core does not grant or imply.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit trust constraints prevent inappropriate privilege inference.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Execution eligibility does not imply administrative, emergency, or data‑policy bypass privileges.
